title: How I used Codex to test offline progression in a Godot idle RPG
author: Knuckleclot
selftext:
i’m building fellvault, a mobile idle rpg in godot. i used codex on two parts of offline progression: reusing the combat rules and making the return screen testable. the tricky part was keeping the result consistent with what someone’s build can actually beat.



here’s the shape we landed on. run adventure on a copy of the save, simulate against the hero’s real stats, and collect the keeper clears separately. the caller then settles the rewards and updates the save. the simulation doesn’t open a battle scene, touch the UI, or save on its own. auto advance gets a limited window (10 minutes, up to three keeper clears). when it hits a wall or the window ends, the remaining time goes toward farming. if the player selected farming, it stays in farming.



what helped was asking codex for scenarios with concrete expected outcomes: already in farm mode, short absence, a hero that can clear the next keeper, and one that loses the first boss fight. i also asked it to exercise the in-game return flow so i could see whether the stage range and loot on the recap agreed with the saved progression. it made the boundaries easier to check every time we adjusted the keeper curve.



for anyone building offline mechanics in godot, how do you cover the gap between a deterministic sim test and a device actually suspending and resuming the app?
